clue.text: Go to the devil for advice Katerina took before she was tamed?

definitions.meaning: an old curse wishing someone ill, as in 'curse you'

definitions.text: advice Katerina took before she was tamed?
definitions.meaning: Katerina is Shakespeare's shrew in The Taming of the Shrew, so the advice she followed was to 'be a shrew'

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare buff wonders what counsel the fiery heroine followed before Petruchio tamed her.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as BE SHREW for the second reading; the whole word is an archaic verb used in curses such as 'Beshrew me!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb is an imprecation, a mild curse damning someone, much like telling them to go to hell.

clue.text: Do anything but meet the challenge front on

definitions.text: Do anything but meet the challenge front on

parts.words: Do anything but meet the challenge front on
parts.note: a phrasal verb for retreating or withdrawing, read as going backwards instead of facing up to a challenge

explanation.surface: Advice to someone ducking a confrontation in any way they can.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat from a confrontation is the opposite of meeting it head on.

clue.text: Subject to one object, does it give the criminal no option?

definitions.meaning: in grammar, a clause with a single subject and predicate, here one object

definitions.text: does it give the criminal no option?
definitions.meaning: a plain prison term with no option of a fine

explanation.surface: A grammar question doubles as a question about a judge's punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' and 'object' look like legal or personal words but are grammar terms; 'no option' means no option of paying a fine instead of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call a one-clause statement this; a court passing straight imprisonment with no fine alternative gives one too.

clue.text: Goldfield making money for South Africa

definitions.meaning: the Witwatersrand, the great gold-mining region near Johannesburg
the South African currency unit

explanation.surface: A gold-mining area supplies a country's wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Witwatersrand mining area gave its short name to the South African currency.

clue.text: Feller may be just a male puppet

definitions.meaning: one who fells trees, a forester or lumberjack
a puppet is a figure carved from wood, so a male one is a wooden man

explanation.surface: A remark that some chap is merely somebody else's puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' reads as slang for a fellow but means one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester who cuts down trees is a feller; a carved wooden figure of a man is a puppet.

clue.text: Effect of boat moving on water between Lincoln and Norfolk

definitions.text: Effect of boat moving on water
definitions.meaning: the disturbed water left behind a moving vessel
the bay on the English east coast lying between Lincolnshire and Norfolk

explanation.surface: A boat cruises along the English east coast stirring up the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln and Norfolk stand for the English counties Lincolnshire and Norfolk; the bay between them is called The Wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves left in a boat's wake are its wake-water; the estuary bay between those counties carries the same name.

clue.text: Part of horse that becomes shrivelled

definitions.meaning: the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades
a verb form meaning dries up or shrinks

explanation.surface: A vet notes some part of a horse is wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse height is measured to the shoulder ridge; a plant that shrivels is said to fade and dry in this way.

clue.text: Leave out the refuse container

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over
a large open bin for builders' rubbish

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the rubbish bin outside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a large open rubbish container left in the street for building waste is called a skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to pass over it; a builder's open rubbish bin has the same name.

clue.text: Give right name to a printer's measure

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width, half an em
a title is a name, as of a book

explanation.surface: Someone assigns the proper heading to a piece of typesetting.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant someone a claim or permission is to empower them.

clue.text: Barrister who found benches clamour disturbing?

indicators.note: disturbing suggests the letters of the words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A lawyer finds the court benches noisy and unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' signals an anagram of BENCHES and CLAMOUR together.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a lawyer who advised in private rooms rather than pleading in court.

clue.text: Admitting being a deb possessed of sex appeal

parts.note: a debutante makes her entry into society, which is called her coming out
having, along with
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A debutante confesses to being very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally confessing or saying something openly is to own up.

clue.text: Where French planes circle the railway

parts.note: a circle is the round letter O
RLY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Aircraft in France fly around above a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Orly is a Paris airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A major airport near Paris, a place where French aircraft land.

clue.text: A birthday honour bestowed by the queen as a warning light

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is awarded in the monarch's Birthday Honours
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A royal honour is awarded as a cautionary signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birthday Honours is the British list of awards announced on the monarch's official birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle traffic signal, an orange light, warns that red is coming.

clue.text: Don't insert the number of Arabian nights in 39 sacred books

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: the Old Testament has 39 books, so OT
the Thousand and One Nights: 1001 in Roman numerals is M and I

explanation.surface: An editor tells someone not to add the Arabian tales to the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 1001 is M (1000) plus I (1), and that pair goes in OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out is the reverse of putting it in.

clue.text: Fielding position for Bradman after ten centuries and a single

indicators.note: after places the cricketer's name behind the other letters

parts.note: ten hundreds make a thousand, M in Roman numerals
one, the Roman numeral I
Sir Donald Bradman, the great Australian batsman, known as the Don

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: where to put Bradman in the field after he's scored many centuries and a single.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side; 'centuries' and 'single' look like batting scores but give M and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where a cricket fielder stands, on the leg side near the bowler.

clue.text: A grain one might find on oak

parts.note: corn is cereal grain

explanation.surface: A seed that turns up on an oak tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree grows on its branches.

clue.text: Angling 'for the secret of atomic power?

definitions.text: Angling 'for the secret of atomic power?

parts.words: Angling 'for the secret of atomic power?
parts.note: angling is 'fishin'', and splitting atoms is the source of nuclear power, so the pun says it as fishing

explanation.surface: A scientist is fishing about for the source of nuclear energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a dropped-g accent, 'fishin'' rings like the nuclear-physics word.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting atomic nuclei releases nuclear energy, the secret of atomic power.

clue.text: What sweat glands do on skin and hide

definitions.text: What sweat glands do on skin
definitions.meaning: to produce and discharge a liquid
to conceal

explanation.surface: A biology note on sweat glands and skin, or animal hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin and hide' reads as a pair of nouns, but 'hide' is the verb meaning to stash away.
explanation.definitionFit: Glands discharge fluid; the same verb also means to stash something away.

clue.text: Wind the week-end up?

definitions.meaning: a seasonal wind bringing heavy rain in South Asia
when the weekend is over, Mon(day) comes soon

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the weekend is over, or whether a gale is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MON SOON: once the weekend is up, Monday is soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal wind of South Asia that brings the rains.

clue.text: Gruesome twisted bar used in war-club

indicators.note: used in places the bent letters inside the weapon

parts.note: a mace is a heavy spiked club used as a weapon

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of the word bar are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim description of a bent metal bar made into a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns BAR into ABR, and 'used in' sets it inside MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ghastly and horrifying, dwelling on death.

clue.text: Ideas currently unattractive in atomic physics

definitions.meaning: thoughts or concepts
not charged particles: ions carry an electric charge and attract

explanation.surface: A remark that some theories have lately fallen out of favour in physics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' looks like 'at present' but means electrically; split the answer as NOT IONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or concepts are notions, the everyday sense.

clue.text: Replacing chair to serve at the bean-feast

indicators.note: replacing means putting the letters back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone moves a chair to serve food at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' signals an anagram of CHAIR and TO; a bean-feast is a British word for a celebration meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of bean, also a mutton stew, served at a bean-feast.

clue.text: Bolt holder of tensile steel for a difficult case

definitions.meaning: a strong steel nut that holds a bolt
a tough person or problem to deal with

explanation.surface: An engineering note on bolts and their steel fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough person is hard to crack, like a strong steel fitting that holds a bolt.

clue.text: Ram into cart smashed by rail vehicle

indicators.note: smashed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ram charges into a cart and wrecks it, struck by a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' signals an anagram of RAM and CART.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar running on rails in the road.

clue.text: In music it is always left after C and before E&F

definitions.text: In music it is always left after C and before E&F

explanation.surface: A music lesson: a symbol always sits at the left, near some notes.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left sits after C and before EF, and the musical sign itself always stands at the left of the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol at the left of a musical staff fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: No bow for a famous violinist

definitions.meaning: the back of a ship, not its front
Isaac ..., the American violinist

explanation.surface: A famous violinist without his bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests a violin bow but means the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of a boat is the opposite of its front; Isaac Stern was a renowned violinist.

clue.text: A nut turns into a prickly pear

indicators.note: turns means the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A nut transforms into a cactus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' signals an anagram of A NUT; the prickly pear cactus fruit is also called by the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of the opuntia cactus is called this in Spanish and in English.

clue.text: A Guildhall giant utterly amazed

parts.note: Gog and Magog are the giant figures in London's Guildhall

explanation.surface: A giant in the London Guildhall is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants whose statues stand in the Guildhall, the City of London's civic hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly excited and astonished, wide-eyed.

clue.text: Novel ending to Nelson's dilemma

indicators.note: ending to points to the closing run of letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Lord Nelson's predicament comes to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters of 'dilemma' give the Jane Austen novel; Nelson's mistress Emma Hamilton was his dilemma too.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: Play?

parts.note: a request for a piece to be performed, or the music heard behind the action of a stage play

explanation.surface: A one-word question.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music played behind the action of a drama or film.

clue.text: Decrepit sage gets older

indicators.note: decrepit means worn and broken down, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old wise man grows older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrepit' signals an anagram of SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning grows old, as a person does.

clue.text: Sleuth film preview

definitions.meaning: one who follows or tracks someone
a short advertisement for a coming film

explanation.surface: A detective film is previewed.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective tails a suspect; a cinema advert gives a sneak look at a coming film.
